newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia still working on De Beers gem deal.
newsitem.headline: Russia still working on De Beers gem deal.

text.p: Talks on a stalled gem trade deal between Russian diamond producer Almazy-Rossii-Sakha (ARS) and De Beers are continuing, but a decision on whether to sign the deal may not be taken on Tuesday, an ARS spokeswoman said.
"All I know is that talks on the deal are continuing," she said. "We had expected agreement on the signing today, but it is still impossible to say exactly when the deal will go through."
Earlier this month ARS said Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais had said that the decision on whether to sign the deal or not would be taken on April 15.
Itar-Tass news agency, quoting a senior government source, also said on Tuesday that a presidential decree, needed before any agreement can come into effect, would be signed within the next 10 days.
"The decree will certainly be signed, as without an agreement we (Russia) are losing out on enormous opportunities," the source was quoted as saying.
He said that there was no problem with the basic content of the draft agreement, but that some "legal nuances" needed further work.
De Beers, frustrated at Moscow's inability to communicate its position on a draft trade agreement submitted to the cabinet in October 1996, stopped buying gems from Russia at the end of last year.

ARS had said earlier that De Beers bought some ARS diamonds in February, but that the South African company was not able to export the diamonds because of Russian government delays in resolving export quota issues, which are part of a stalled deal.
